starting_points.name: Official create-astro basics template
starting_points.when: A new content-first site has repeatable pages, typed content or selective interactive components and can start with static output.
steps: Use an unused source directory outside synchronized storage. Read project requirements and decide whether source content belongs in Git or an already-selected headless CMS.

Check current Astro Node requirements and inspect create-astro help before selecting flags. For the tested create-astro 5.3.1 CLI, the command below generated the basics template with no package installation, Git initialization or AI instruction files.

Install dependencies in the generated project with the selected package manager. Record resolved create-astro, Astro, Node and package-manager versions, commit the lockfile, and retain generated scripts and configuration.
Create explicit page routes for content. If a collection should produce one URL per entry, define a schema and a dynamic route using getStaticPaths; collection files alone do not create pages.
Review public routes, canonical site URL, trailing slashes, redirects, sitemap, 404 behavior and static asset paths before connecting the intended host.

commands.purpose: Generate the official basics project without installing dependencies, initializing Git or creating AI instruction files.
Install the dependencies generated by the CLI and create the package lockfile.

notes: The tested CLI version was create-astro 5.3.1; it resolved Astro 7.4.2 from the template. The command-line `--no-ai` option came from the installed CLI help; confirm it remains supported before reusing this command.
Replace my-site with the intended unused directory. `@latest` is a scaffold-time lookup; pin the selected runtime through project policy and use the generated lockfile for later installs.

The disposable qualification used Node 24.21.0 and npm 11.19.0. It ran `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1`, and fetched `/` with HTTP 200 and `text/html`. This only verifies the untouched basics starter, not an application, integration, CMS, adapter or production host.
The project README remains the owner of purpose, start commands and content/workflow navigation. Do not create or rely on project AGENTS.md files.

follow_up_generators.name: Content Collections
follow_up_generators.when: Markdown or structured content needs a validated schema and generated pages; do not add a collection layer for a handful of stable one-off pages.
steps: Define the content shape and source owner before writing a schema. Use local files for Git-reviewed content or fetch from the selected CMS without changing that CMS's editorial ownership.
Create the collection schema and an explicit route template. Call getCollection and getStaticPaths to create static URLs for entries; verify the final route names and content output.
Test malformed content at build time and check empty, draft and missing-route behavior. Preview/editor access is a separate CMS integration and authorization concern.
notes: Astro validates collection entries against schemas and generates TypeScript support, but collection entries do not become pages automatically.
If editors need a visual workflow, select a headless CMS and define ownership for drafts, preview, approvals, publishing hooks and media. Astro itself is not that editorial interface.

follow_up_generators.name: Server adapter
follow_up_generators.when: A specific route needs request-time rendering, request cookies/headers or private personalization, and the selected host/runtime can operate the chosen adapter.
notes: Read the current adapter guide and the selected host's support limits before adding it. Astro's default output is static; on-demand rendering requires an adapter.

This profile does not add database, authentication, API, email or durable-job ownership. Keep those responsibilities in their existing backend unless they are separately designed, migrated and tested.
Qualify adapter behavior, secrets, cookies, headers, caching, redirects, cold starts and deployment independently. The static starter build does not establish any of these properties.

follow_up_generators.name: Interactive island integration
follow_up_generators.when: A content route has a defined widget whose stateful behavior justifies a component framework, and the team has selected that framework.
notes: Use semantic HTML and browser APIs first. Add only the chosen official Astro integration (for example, React, Svelte or Vue) and hydrate only the component that needs browser interaction.
Keep content output usable as HTML. A client island does not supply backend authorization, persistence or offline synchronization.

preserve: Generated package scripts, Astro configuration, TypeScript settings, project lockfile and ignore rules; record any intentional change in README.
Content collection schemas, route templates, public URL policy and CMS/API ownership as editable project sources.
Original media sources and attribution records; use src assets for processing or public assets for deliberate unprocessed direct URLs.
verification: Run npm ci and npm run build with the committed lockfile; a successful untouched starter build does not qualify a site's content or integrations.
Run npm run dev and inspect generated pages and routes. Check route HTML, collection entry URLs, missing pages, assets and browser behavior.

Set the real site URL and verify canonical metadata and sitemap against production host configuration. Check redirect status and trailing-slash behavior at that host; static output may express redirects as HTML rather than an HTTP status.
Verify image transformations and direct public asset URLs. If video is used, test its chosen streaming service and do not attribute video handling to Astro.

If adding an adapter or CMS, test its actual preview, draft privacy, authorization, cookies, redirects, runtime APIs, cache behavior and production deployment separately. No application integration test or static regression suite was run for this record.
integration_steps: From the generated project root, write README purpose, start commands, content source and editorial owner, public URL policy and navigation to installed Astro documentation. Preserve the user's existing repository instructions.

Create Content Collections only when structured Markdown/data needs schema validation; define the schema and explicit static page routes together. Keep static public content distinct from draft or account-specific content.

Document the content-route and URL map, canonical domain, trailing-slash rule, 404 behavior, redirects and the host setting that implements each. Confirm whether static redirect output provides the required response status; if not, configure a host redirect rule or select an adapter route and verify it.

Set the production site URL and generate a sitemap only when required. Review canonical URLs, duplicate routes, metadata, indexability and actual generated HTML; SEO metadata does not establish search indexing.

Assign media ownership explicitly. Use src image imports for supported processing, public files for unprocessed stable paths, and a selected external service for video streaming. Check license, alt text, dimensions, cache and delivery on the deployed host.

For a selected CMS, keep the CMS authoritative for editorial content, drafts and assets. Specify build/webhook ownership, preview and draft authorization before connecting it; do not leak preview tokens into client islands or static output.

Keep existing APIs, identity, database, migrations, jobs and external effects with their current owners. A static Astro client can consume public or authenticated API endpoints as designed, but static files cannot contain secrets or provide request-time permission checks. If a server-side page or new API is required, define a separate backend/adapter migration and its data ownership before implementation.

Run the project build and dev server; inspect generated route HTML, direct URLs, assets and not-found behavior. Against the intended host, verify redirect status, headers, cache, canonical URL and sitemap. This research did not run application tests, a CMS integration or an adapter deployment.
